text:
maria: Quick sync — I need a 90s battlecard + 3 slide webinar snippet that differentiates Redwood vs cloud AI platforms and managed LLM APIs. Focus on marketing copy + one benchmark nugget.
jonathan: Sounds good. Priority: latency predictability and cost controls. Two one-liners: 'Predictable inference economics at any scale' and 'Same API from hosted to on‑prem'.
sarah: For benchmarks: use our 95th pct latency + cost per 1k tokens with caching enabled. Eg: '95th pct < 120ms on chat workloads vs X's 300ms in our internal test.' Keep the language careful — say 'internal benchmark' and link to notes.
lee: Sales needs a routing play: inbound leads > ask for tier (SaaS vs regulated) > auto-route to solutions_eng if private deployment. Add a short qualifier question: 'Do you need on-prem or VPC controls?'
maria: Perfect. Can we draft 3 headline options and a 1-paragraph claim + evidence for each? I'll loop design.
jonathan: Drafts:
1) Headline: 'Production-first LLM serving for engineering teams'
   Claim: 'Ship LLM features with predictable latency, cost, and fallbacks.'
   Evidence: 'Unified API across hosted, dedicated, private; KV cache + batching; automatic model fallback.'
2) Headline: 'Lower unit cost without losing quality'
   Claim: 'Smart caching & batching cuts per-token costs while preserving SLOs.'
   Evidence: 'Selective quantization + prefix caching saved 30% in X workload (internal test).'
3) Headline: 'Keep features online under load'
   Claim: 'Graceful degradation with model variants and cross-region fallback.'
   Evidence: 'Canary rollouts and automatic fallback reduced error windows in our chaos run.'
sarah: Love 1 and 3. For the webinar snippet pick 1 + quick demo of failover routing and a side-by-side latency chart. Add a callout: 'how we measure: tokenized prompt distribution, tail-latency SLOs.'
lee: For the battlecard summary for sales: 2 short competitor rebuttals:
- vs Cloud AI: 'They expose endpoints but lack unified private deployment story + invariant API.'
- vs Managed LLM APIs: 'Many prioritize model catalog; Redwood prioritizes serving economics and ops controls.'
maria: Add an inbound routing script for SDRs:
"Hi {name}, quick Q: are you evaluating for latency & cost, compliance (VPC/on‑prem), or throughput?"
If latency/cost -> link to benchmark page; if compliance -> escalate to solutions_eng; if throughput -> invite to Dedicated capacity FAQ.
jonathan: Also include a nugget for the webinar registration page: 'See live demo: 3-min failover + 2-min cost comparison' — short and tangible.
sarah: Action items: maria will draft slide copy + 90s battlecard; jonathan to attach internal benchmark CSV and method; lee to write SDR routing script; I'll proof and add legal-safe language.
maria: Timeline: draft by EOD today, review tomorrow 10am. @deploy-bot can you post the benchmark CSV link once jonathan uploads?
deploy-bot: benchmark CSV uploaded to #private-artifacts: s3://redwood-internal/benchmarks/1905-webinar.csv :white_check_mark:
lee: got it, I'll start the SDR playbook snippet now.
maria: thanks team — feel free to drop quick edits here. :thumbsup:
